descriptionChirho: The masculine proper noun חֲשַׁבְיָה / חֲשַׁבְיָהוּ (meaning 'Yah(u) has taken account, Yahweh has reckoned') designating several Levites and officials in post-exilic literature. The name appears in both its short form חֲשַׁבְיָה (Hashabiah/Chashavyah) and the longer theophoric form חֲשַׁבְיָהוּ (Chashavyahu/Hashabyahu). Individuals bearing this name include: a temple musician (1 Chr 25:3, 19), a Levite in David's administration (1 Chr 6:45; 9:14; 26:30; 27:17), Levites in Ezra's caravan (Ezra 8:19, 24), officials in Nehemiah's Jerusalem (Neh 3:17; 10:11; 11:15, 22; 12:21, 24). The variant spellings and prepositional forms (לַחֲשַׁבְיָה 'for Hashabiah,' וַחֲשַׁבְיָהוּ 'and Hashabiah') are inflectional, not distinct senses. Multilingual transliterations confirm a single referent type: Arabic حَشَبْيا, German Haschabja, Korean 하샤비야/하사비야, Spanish Hasabías/Jasabya, Hindi हशब्याह, French Hashabia.
